thread.title: Oprah Winfrey Wins the First Quarter

author: Barron's
title: Oprah Winfrey Wins the First Quarter
text:
In a largely flat quarter, small-cap stocks held up slightly better than bigger ones, quality did slightly better than high risk, and those overseas did slightly better than those in the U.S.
Christopher Polk/Getty Images The broad MSCI USA Small Cap Index posted a negative return of 0.5% (including reinvested dividends) over the quarter. A loss is a loss, but this was ahead of the blue chips. The MSCI USA Index of large- and mid-cap U.S. stocks lost 0.8%.
Sure, the difference is marginal. But typically Wall Street expects bigger companies to hold up better in a troubled market. This time around, worries about global trade, and downdrafts hitting such large-company titans as Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ), and Facebook ( FB ), hurt the big stocks.
Among small companies, higher-quality names-such as those with track records of actually making a profit-did better than more-speculative issues. The S&P SmallCap 600 index , which excludes many of the riskiest names, outperformed the broader Russell 2000 small-cap index by 0.6% over the quarter.
Still, U.S. small-cap stocks were the worst performers of the three main categories used by investors, trailing their peers' returns in developed overseas markets (such as Europe and Japan) and those in emerging markets.
The -0.5% negative return from MSCI U.S. small-caps compared to a 0.0% dead break-even for the MSCI Emerging Markets Small Cap Index , and a 0.05% gain for the MSCI EAFE Index of small-cap international stocks in Europe, Australasia, and the Far East.
As it happens, Russian small-cap stocks were among the best performers in the world, with the MSCI Russia Small Cap Index returning 5.6% in U.S. dollar terms. Vladimir Putin's international pariah status doesn't seem to be hurting the bottom line.
Among other strong performers, the MSCI Singapore Small Cap Index rose 4.2%, and that of Brazil, 5.3%.
Meanwhile, back here at home, Fossil Group ( FOSL ), the fashion-accessory and watch maker, and Nutrisystem ( NTRI ), the diet company, were among the notable small-cap performers. Both win a Flying Omelet award for splattering the most egg on Wall Street faces.
According to FactSet data, Nutrisystem began the year with a solid slate of Buy recommendations from analysts-and then fell 48% in three months. Among the problems: competing with Oprah Winfrey , who is keeping rival Weight Watchers International (WTW) on a roll.
Fossil, for its part, has risen an astonishing 65% since Jan. 1. Yet according to FactSet, bulls were rare indeed on the Street before this remarkable rise. Of the analysts who cover the stock, more than 90% rated it a Hold or Sell. Sell notes, unusually, outnumbered Buy recommendations by three to one.
